drug_class: MET inhibitor (targeted cancer therapy / kinase inhibitor)
purpose: Capmatinib is used to treat a certain type of non-small cell lung cancer in adults. It is specifically for people whose cancer has a mutation in a gene called MET, which is causing the cancer to grow. Your doctor will test your tumor to confirm this mutation before starting treatment.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have an abnormal change (mutation) in a gene called MET that sends signals telling the cancer to grow and spread. Capmatinib works by blocking this MET signal, like putting a plug in the cancer's growth switch. This helps slow or stop the cancer from growing without affecting many normal cells.
common_side_effects: Swelling in your legs, hands, or face (edema); feeling sick to your stomach (nausea); feeling very tired; shortness of breath; decreased appetite; vomiting; and increased creatinine levels in your blood tests. Some people also experience back pain or cough.
warnings: Capmatinib can cause serious lung problems (interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis) — call your doctor right away if you develop new or worsening shortness of breath or cough. It can harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is essential during treatment and for a period after. It may also cause liver problems, sensitivity to sunlight (use sunscreen and protective clothing), and can affect your kidneys. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take as interactions are possible.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 400 mg taken by mouth twice a day (about every 12 hours), with or without food. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or split them. Try to take it at the same times each day. If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time — do not take a double dose.
